name: Ratings [✓]
description:
Professional rating system for Jellyfin. Rate media with 1-10 stars, view detailed user ratings on hover, and see rating badges on media cards. Optimized for large libraries with lazy loading.  
  
Universal Repo 
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/K3ntas/jellyfin-plugin-ratings/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/K3ntas/jellyfin-plugin-ratings
overview: Comprehensive rating plugin with star-based UI, average ratings display, detailed user rating popups, and performance-optimized card overlays for large media libraries.

versions.changelog: A new series gives one notification instead of one per episode. New episodes of a series you already have are grouped into one notification per season, showing which episodes arrived. Clicking a request pop-up opens that request, or the media once it is available.

Rating 10 is easier to reach. The red count on the request (+) button works on Jellyfin 12. Admins get a pop-up when someone makes a request, and users get one when their request is fulfilled. New-media pop-ups show posters and episode details again on Jellyfin 12.

Admins can remove any review. Users can hide their profile. New settings to turn off reviews and the Other Users tab. Ratings under 1 now save. Duplicates: Keep both button, correct series sizes, and no more false matches on music named "Track 01". Revision History updated.

Removes the "Unknown" cards with a blank poster and a "Not on server" tag from profiles. They were ratings of media that has since been deleted from the server and was rated before the plugin started remembering titles and posters, so there was nothing to show but the stars. They are now left out of the profile grid, reviews and activity. Deleted media that the plugin remembers keeps showing with its title and poster, as before. Nothing is deleted: if the media comes back to the library, its rating shows up again.

Fixes the stars and the reviews section appearing on library pages. Opening a library such as "Movies" or "TV Shows" from its header shows it on a details page, the same layout a movie uses, so the rating widget and "User Reviews" were added there too. People rated and reviewed the library itself, and the page then said you had rated "TV Shows". Libraries and folders no longer show the widget, and the server refuses a rating for them.

Adds a "Remove ratings left on libraries" button to the plugin's settings page, under the Jellyfin rating sync options. Updating does not delete ratings people already left on a library, and with the stars gone from library pages they could no longer remove them themselves. The button shows how many there are and on which libraries, including how many have a written review, and deletes them only after you confirm. The review text goes with them. Ratings on movies and shows are not touched.

Fixes plugin updates not reaching the browser at all. After updating, the page kept running the previous version's code, so everything fixed in a release looked like it had never been released, and only a manual hard refresh brought it through. The plugin adds its script tag to the page as Jellyfin sends it, but when the browser asked whether its copy of the page was still current, Jellyfin answered "unchanged" without sending the page - so there was nothing to add the tag to, and the browser reused its stored copy, still pointing at the old version's script, which is cached for a year on purpose and so was never re-requested. The page is now always sent in full and is no longer stored by the browser, so a new version shows up on the next ordinary page load. The large script and stylesheet keep their long-term caching.

Fixes the dashboard's Plugins page showing "An error occurred while loading plugins" after updating. Cleaning up the previous version's leftover folder removed it while Jellyfin was still running and still had it listed, and every later look at the plugin catalogue tried to write into a folder that was no longer there, which failed the whole page until Jellyfin was restarted. Only Linux and Docker servers were affected - on Windows the old files stay locked, so the folder was never actually removed. The cleanup now hands the old folder to Jellyfin to remove, the same way its own uninstall does.

Ratings can now be given to one decimal place from the rating window, not just from the stars on the movie page. Moving across the big stars shows the decimal you are about to pick and clicking takes it - 5.4, not 5 - and swiping on a phone does the same, with the star you stop on filled part-way to match. Previously each big star was a separate button, so the rating window could only ever give whole numbers. A decimal picked on the movie page also arrives in the window drawn correctly instead of being rounded down.

"No reviews yet. Be the first to write one!" is now a button. It looked like a caption, so people clicked it, nothing happened, and they scrolled back up to find the stars. It carries a pencil, highlights when you point at it, and opens the rating and review window.

Fixes a review not appearing after you write it. The review was always saved - the block of reviews further down the page just never re-read itself, so it kept showing whatever was there when the page opened, and the review only turned up once you had navigated away and back. That is why writing it a second time seemed to work: the first one had taken all along. The reviews now refresh as soon as a rating or review is added, changed or removed. A review written moments ago also used to be labelled "-1 days ago" instead of "Today", because the server stamps the time from its own clock and being a fraction of a second ahead of the browser was enough to push the age below zero.

Also fixes stale plugin folders being left behind after an update, mostly on Windows, where the old copy's file stays locked until Jellyfin restarts. The previous attempt deleted the old folder's meta.json to take it out of circulation, which turns out to do the opposite: Jellyfin treats a plugin folder with no meta.json as an active plugin named after the folder and loads it anyway. The result was two copies of this plugin running at once - doubled up services and duplicate endpoints, with the old copy able to answer requests - and a folder this plugin could no longer recognise in order to clean up. An old folder that cannot be deleted is now marked as deleted in its own manifest instead, which is what Jellyfin does itself: it is not loaded, and Jellyfin removes the folder at a later restart. Folders already left in the broken state are picked up and finished off.

Fixes the admin Ratings dashboard on Jellyfin 12, where every panel read "Failed to load" and the counters stayed empty. The dashboard's own pages were still identifying themselves the older way that Jellyfin 12 no longer accepts; they now use the current form, which Jellyfin 10.x accepts just as well, so one build covers both. The version shown at the top of the dashboard is now read from the plugin that is actually running instead of being typed into the page, so it can no longer drift out of date. The phone header also had a pass. Opening the plugin menu now keeps every button on a single line all the way down to a narrow phone, on a panel that spans the screen with even margins and rounded ends instead of sitting flush against one edge. The menu button and the account picture next to it were brought down to the size of everything else in the row, and while the menu is open the heading and the row-scrolling arrows underneath step out of sight so nothing shows through it. Closing it puts them straight back. The plugin's dialogs - media management, duplicates and the full ratings list - now fit inside a phone screen instead of pushing the page sideways.

A rebuilt rating system with real precision. Until now every rating was one of ten fixed steps, so a film was a 7 or an 8 with nothing in between. The whole star row is now a single sliding control: move across it and the stars fill smoothly under your pointer, a tenth of a star at a time, with the exact value appearing beside them as you go. Give something a 7.5 when 7 feels harsh and 8 feels generous. On a phone, swipe along the stars for the same control. The value appears while you are choosing and steps out of the way once you are done, so nothing clutters the page, and a deliberate press is still what saves a rating - simply passing over the stars never changes one you have already given. Everything you have rated before carries over untouched, and whole numbers work exactly as they always did.

Brings the header buttons back on Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin 12 rebuilt its web interface, and while it still leaves the old header in the page it collapses it to nothing - so the buttons were being created into something invisible. They now go into the new header, in the same place as before: immediately left of Jellyfin's own cast and search icons. The collapsed menu on phones is unchanged, and the buttons now also survive moving around the app, including in and out of the admin dashboard, which previously lost them until a manual refresh. Nothing changes on Jellyfin 10.x, where the old header is still used.

Fixes the plugin on Jellyfin 12, where every panel read "Failed to load" and film pages showed "Error loading ratings" (issue #83). Jellyfin 12 switched off the older ways of proving who you are and the plugin was still using them, so the server refused each request even though you were signed in - while the public files it serves kept working, which is why the interface still appeared but had no data in it. It now asks the way Jellyfin 12 expects; older Jellyfin versions accept the same form, so this one build works on both and there is nothing to choose when installing. Also stops the activity feed, top rated list and browse-by-rating from naming titles that live in libraries an account is not allowed to open.

Fixes the friends list showing "Failed to load friends" for anyone who actually had friends (issue #79). The list was loading correctly - it crashed while drawing the first friend, and that crash was being reported as a loading failure. A user with no friends never hit it, which is why it took a report to find. The panel now explains what went wrong instead of showing one generic line, offers a Retry, and is translated in every language. In media management you can also choose which copy of a duplicate to keep (issue #80) - press Keep this on any copy and the bin moves to the others, which matters when identical copies sit on different drives.

Finishes the translation work and adds a security pass. An audit of the whole plugin found another 141 phrases written straight into the markup - the profile settings window, the rating box, review comments, the media picker and its sort menu, friend menus, chat controls, moderator and ban dialogs, and every "nothing here yet" message. All of them are translated now, in all fifteen languages, and each pack carries around 560 phrases where it had about 348. On security: no exploitable weakness was found, and three things were tightened. Profile header uploads now check the file really is a GIF, MP4 or WEBM rather than trusting its name, since the address serving them is public by design. Bug report screenshots are fetched with your access token in a header instead of the web address, keeping it out of browser history. And asking for better quality now respects each account's library access. The dashboard heading also shows the right version again.

The profile page, the friends panel and the star rating widget are translated at last. Those three areas were never connected to the translation system - the words were written straight into the markup - so they stayed in English no matter which language you picked, in all sixteen languages. Forty-seven labels now go through the translation layer and are filled in for every language: the friends panel and its tabs, the profile tab strip and stat row, follow, block and friend buttons, the rating popup, and the whole sidebar down to Stats, Films, Shows, Hours, Taste, Similar Taste, Add a film, Back, Member since and the "not on server" badge. The thirty-eight strings from the quality-request and bug-report queues are translated too. Every language pack gains eighty-five entries. Thanks to chosqui for reporting it in discussion #76 with a Spanish patch that showed exactly what was missing.

Three fixes to the support queues added last release, all found by using them on a real server. The Quality and Bug Reports tabs never appeared in the Request Media window: that window is built in more than one place in the client and only one of them had been given the new tabs, so the two queues had no way in. Opening a request or a report drew the detail window underneath the one it was launched from, which made clicking a Quality row look as though nothing happened at all. And people who sent a bug report had no way of telling whether anyone had looked at it - the report box now lists your own reports beneath it with their status and any reply, and sending one no longer closes the window, so the report lands in that list in front of you. Note: after updating, reload the page with the cache cleared. The browser holds on to the page that references the previous version of the plugin's script, and until it lets go you will still be running the old one.

Two new ways for people to tell you something is wrong, and one place to work through both. A Better Quality tab on the profile searches what is already on the server, and every result carries a button to say what is wrong with the current copy - blurry, wrong audio, missing subtitles. A Report a problem button next to Edit Profile takes a description plus screenshots, pasted straight from the clipboard or picked from disk. Both land in the Request Media window as their own tabs, badged with how many are still open, where you can read the report, look at the screenshots, reply to the person who sent it, and mark it solved or declined - your reply is shown back to them. This release also fixes a profile showing 0 films and 0 hours next to a taste chart reporting hundreds of hours: those figures came from ratings alone, so anyone who watches without rating saw zeros. They now count what you have watched as well as what you have rated. And the genre breakdown was the one part of a profile with no privacy check, so a private profile's viewing habits could be read by anyone signed in.

The request list in the admin panel now lays out properly on a phone. Each request kept its title, user, date and status on a single row, so on a narrow screen the title was squeezed down to a few characters, and the media-link and rejection-reason boxes were split across a width that could not hold them. The title now takes a line of its own with the details underneath it, the expand arrow sits at the right edge, and the two input boxes stack at full width. Reported and written by @daki456. The input rules also apply in every language now - they previously keyed off the English placeholder text, so they did nothing on a translated server.

Fixes the request list in the admin panel. A category holding more requests than fit on screen squashed its cards down into unreadable slivers instead of scrolling - the cards were being compressed to fit the available height rather than keeping their own. Each category now scrolls once it passes 500 pixels, with the cards at their normal size. Thanks to @daki456 for reporting and fixing it.

Leftover trickplay cleanup now covers both ways Jellyfin stores it. Libraries set to 'save trickplay images next to media' keep the tiles in a folder beside each video rather than in the central directory, and those were invisible to the previous scan - a server using that setting appeared to have no trickplay at all. Both places are now scanned and cleaned, and the panel reports what it found in each. Verified on a live library: it correctly identified real leftovers from deleted media while leaving every folder whose video is still present untouched.

Fixes the leftover-trickplay cleanup, which previously reported nothing to clean up on every server. Jellyfin stores trickplay in folders grouped by the first two characters of each item id, and the scan was treating one of those groups as the whole directory - so it looked at a single group out of 256, usually an empty one. It now reads the real directory and looks inside every group. The panel also showed internal labels instead of readable text, and now names the directory it checked and how many folders it examined, so 'nothing to clean up' can be told apart from a scan that never ran.

Two clean-ups from the security review. Searching and browsing through the plugin now respects the libraries each account is allowed to see, so a user with limited access can no longer come across titles from libraries they cannot open - this affected the plugin's own search, the sorted library view and the latest-media list. Playback was never affected. And when the plugin refuses an action because you are not an administrator, it now says so properly instead of returning a server error; access was already correctly denied, but the message was wrong. Privacy defaults are unchanged - profiles remain visible to everyone unless the user chooses otherwise.

Security and features. Fixes three ways a user could have got script to run inside someone else's session: one through a profile's favourite films, which affected anyone viewing that profile, and two through links attached to media and deletion requests, which ran in an administrator's session. Also closes several privacy and permission gaps - private profiles could be read through the newer profile endpoints, a private list could be read by copying it, direct messages ignored blocking, the recent-requests list showed every user's requests to non-administrators, and a user banned from playback or over quota could bypass both by sending their login token in a different but equally valid form. New: leftover trickplay data can now be cleared from Media Management, so space used by tiles belonging to deleted media can be recovered without reprocessing everything you still have. Search now ignores punctuation and spacing, so 'xfiles', 'x files' and 'X-Files' all find the same show. Ratings can be edited or removed from the Ratings tab, including titles not on the server; reviews can be written for those titles; custom profile rows can be reordered; and any rating can be agreed or disagreed with, not only ones with a written review. The Reviews tab now shows posters. Fixes the empty gap under the header on phones, the plugin's buttons covering the video player in portrait, and missing posters in Recent Activity. Every endpoint now identifies you the same way, so apps signing in with a plain token are no longer refused.

Profile favourites and Media Management fixes. Adding a title from the catalog to a favourites row now works and stays: the button no longer ignores films whose name contains an apostrophe, the card is no longer discarded when you reopen the profile, and rows containing only catalog titles now show them straight away instead of only after adding something else. Titles lost by the earlier fault need re-adding once. Media Management was showing no posters, no media type and dashes for rating, plays, size and status - it now reads every field correctly, and the same fault is fixed on the Scheduled tab, the 'Leaving in' badges, and the media request and ban screens. Media that Jellyfin has not identified, which has no artwork at all, now falls back to a poster from TMDB where one can be found. On phones the header menu is now a compact row of icons rather than one full-width row per button, which previously left most buttons unreachable, plus a layout fix for the ElegantFin skin that is applied only on servers actually using it.

Fixes rating a film that is not on the server failing with a not-authenticated error. Four endpoints checked the signed-in user in a stricter way than the rest of the plugin and rejected perfectly valid requests - rating a TMDB title, reading your own rating for an item, the batch rating lookup used to draw badges, and listing or creating media requests. They now identify you the same way every other endpoint does, so any client sending a valid token is accepted.

Fixes new media being announced but never appearing in the Latest Media list. The list was ordered by the date Jellyfin takes from the file itself, not by when the media actually reached your server - so anything copied in keeping its original timestamps sorted to wherever that old date fell, usually past the end of the list. You would get the 'now available' notification and then find nothing there. The list now also includes everything the plugin announced, dated by when it actually saw it, so the notification and the list can no longer disagree. Items removed from the server since being announced are left out.

Further hardening of the watching hover card, following up the security fix in the previous version. The card no longer reads any text back out of the page at all - the title it shows while loading now comes from data the plugin already holds. Re-inserting text taken from the page undoes whatever escaping made it safe, so the read was removed rather than escaped. Numbers shown on the card (year, running time, score) are also validated as numbers before being displayed, which additionally stops an unexpected value breaking the card.

Security fix. The hover card that shows what someone is watching built an image tag by pasting an item id straight into HTML, and that id was read back out of the page. A crafted value could have escaped the image tag and run script for another user viewing the profile. Item ids are now rejected unless they are genuine Jellyfin ids, and the image is created as a real element instead of being assembled from text, so nothing untrusted can reach the markup. Reported by GitHub CodeQL (js/xss-through-dom, high severity).

API fixes for third-party and TV clients. Social endpoints previously accepted only the raw X-Emby-Token header, so any app using Jellyfin's standard authentication got 401 from every social call while the identical request worked against the ratings API - they now accept every form Jellyfin does, including API keys. All responses are also camelCase now; some endpoints returned PascalCase and others camelCase, which silently produced empty fields in other clients. Your existing data is unaffected. New endpoints make a profile page far cheaper to build: one aggregated profile call instead of nine, ratings/reviews/activity that already include title, poster and year, a per-user rating histogram, a capability check, and paging on followers and following. Nothing changes in the web interface.

Hover what someone is watching to see the poster and details. Pointing at the title in the Similar Taste list now brings up a card with the artwork, year, running time, age rating, community score, genres and a synopsis - so you can tell what it is without leaving the profile. For an episode it shows the series artwork and the episode name. Details are fetched once and remembered for the rest of the session.

Live presence, full titles, and a Watch too button. The Similar Taste list now updates by itself when someone comes online or starts watching - you no longer have to close and reopen the profile to see it. What someone is watching moved onto its own line, so long series titles are readable in full instead of being squeezed between the name and the match percentage. And each person who is watching now has a Watch too button: press it and you are asked whether to join them at the point they are at right now, or start from the beginning.

See who is online and what they are watching, and a much better looking profile name. The Similar Taste list now shows a dot on each person: bright green and pulsing means they are watching something right now, and the card shows what it is with a clock that ticks along live; soft green means online but not watching; grey means offline. The profile name has also been fixed - it was drawn as a colour gradient clipped to the letters, which over a photo or video header turned it into washed-out grey. It is now solid white with proper display typography, using each platform's large-text typeface.

See what you actually watch, find people with the same taste, and Back now works properly. Profiles have a new Taste ring in the sidebar showing your genre breakdown by real watch time - taken from what you have actually played, not just what you rated - with total hours and a percentage per genre. Below it, a Similar Taste list ranks everyone on the server by how closely their genre mix matches yours, showing the genres you have most in common; click anyone to open their profile, or use the envelope button to message them directly. Also fixed: opening someone's profile from a followers or match list and pressing Back used to close the whole profile window instead of returning to the profile you came from.

Rate films that are not on the server, keep ratings readable after media is deleted, choose your TMDB search language, and browse other users. You can now rate a title added to a profile row from the catalog even though it is not on the server - hover it and press Rate. If it is added to the library later, your rating attaches to it automatically. Ratings also remember the title, year and poster of what you rated, so deleting a film no longer leaves a nameless row of stars behind; older ratings fill this in as you use them. Admins can set the language TMDB search returns titles in (Settings, TMDB Search Language) instead of always getting English. And profiles have a new Other Users tab listing everyone on the server, with a filter box, so you can find and visit other people's profiles without knowing their name in advance.

Header buttons now fold into a dropdown menu on phones. With search, language, profile, requests, notifications, latest media, chat and friends all in the header there was simply not enough room on a small screen, and buttons ended up clipped or wrapping badly. On phone-sized screens they now sit behind a single arrow button and open as a tidy list, with the search box at full width. Unread chat messages light a dot on that button so you can still tell something is waiting inside. Nothing changes on tablets or desktop. Thanks to @chosqui for the suggestion (discussion #71).

Fixes from reported issues. The Save button in Profile Settings now works - it was calling an address the server does not accept, so nothing was ever saved, and the privacy tick-boxes always looked switched on regardless of your real settings (#72). The search bar no longer disappears on phones held in portrait: it shrinks to just the magnifier icon and expands when tapped, instead of being hidden on any screen under 400px wide (#69). Deleting media now also removes its trickplay thumbnails and any extracted subtitles or attachments, which used to be left behind forever (#70). Uninstalling the plugin now really removes the header buttons - the plugin no longer edits Jellyfin's index.html, and it cleans up that edit if an older version made one, so users no longer have to clear their browser cache by hand (#66). When an old plugin folder cannot be deleted on Windows because its file is locked, the plugin now removes that folder's meta.json so the stale version stops being listed and loaded (#67). New-media notifications now log why an item was treated as new, to make the remaining reports diagnosable (#65).

Much smaller downloads and far less disk activity. The plugin's script, stylesheet and language files are now sent pre-compressed, so a first page load transfers roughly 108 KB instead of 676 KB - about six times less. This applies even if you reach Jellyfin over HTTPS directly, where Jellyfin's own compression is off by default. Separately, rapid saves are now merged into a single write: previously every user's presence heartbeat rewrote the entire online-users file, so a few people online meant constant disk churn. Nothing is lost - pending saves are flushed on shutdown and before any backup export or import.

Big speed and smoothness pass. Pages load about a third lighter: the plugin's styles are now a proper stylesheet instead of being stuffed inside the script, and only your own language is downloaded rather than all sixteen. Scrolling through libraries is noticeably smoother because the plugin no longer re-scans the whole page every time anything on it changes. The admin Media list now asks the database for just the page you're looking at instead of loading your entire library first, so it opens quickly even on large collections. Chat only fetches new messages instead of re-downloading the last 50 every two seconds, and background tabs stop polling entirely. Watching something no longer rewrites a settings file every few seconds of playback. Data files are also written more safely, so a crash or power cut mid-save can no longer leave them corrupted. Includes the admin category list scrollbar fix from PR #73.

Properly fixes the 'new media' pop-ups that kept appearing for films and shows already on your server. The plugin now learns your whole existing library the first time it runs and only alerts you about genuinely new additions. A library scan, a re-scan, or installing the plugin on a big existing collection no longer floods you with 'now available' alerts for old content - including whole seasons that were already there. Re-scans and re-added files no longer fool it either.

Your ratings now live in Jellyfin too, plus a compatibility fix. Every rating you give is also saved into Jellyfin's own rating, so other apps and tools (like Maintainerr) can find and use your ratings. A one-time 'Sync existing ratings to Jellyfin' button in the plugin settings copies all your past ratings across in one click; new ratings are saved automatically. There's also an optional setting to write the average score into each item's Community Rating (off by default - it replaces the existing IMDb/TMDB score and is undone when Jellyfin refreshes metadata). Fix: the Friends panel (Online tab, friend search) and live chat no longer throw errors on the latest Jellyfin (10.11.10/10.11.11).

Big profile update plus speed and fixes. Faster Latest Media and browsing on large libraries. Hover the rating stars to see the number inside the star. New admin option to show/hide the rating badge on poster cards. Add films/shows that are NOT on the server to your profile rows - drag them in from search or Recent Activity, hover for a Request button. Drag any search result (on-server or catalog) straight into a row. Hover any poster or search result to see its full title, year and description. Upload your own looping GIF or video to show behind your profile name and picture. Fixes: deleting a duplicate now really removes the file (no more reappearing), the rating number no longer sticks after you move off a star, header text stays readable over a video background, and dragging from Recent Activity now reliably sticks.

Speed and reliability improvements. Made the 'Latest Media' panel and general browsing noticeably faster on large libraries by removing heavy background work that ran every minute. Fixed old movies and shows sometimes appearing as 'newly added' when they were not - now only genuinely new media triggers a notification, and the same item is never announced twice (even after a server restart). Fixed custom sorting showing no cards when several folders are combined into one library view.

Faster loading and a duplicate-finder fix. Pages now open quicker: the plugin's add-on is cached by your browser and packaged about a third smaller, so it doesn't re-download every time. Also fixed the Duplicates tool wrongly flagging whole TV shows as duplicates (it was treating every episode of a series as a copy) - it now only groups true duplicates.
Security and cleanup: removed an old, unused profile page that triggered security warnings. The profile you actually use and all other features are unchanged.

Big profile update. Build your profile your way with favorite rows you can name, drag to reorder, and drag posters straight from your recent activity. Search any film or show — watch it if it's on the server, or request it in one click if it isn't. Your ratings, reviews and activity now show the real titles, and you can like or dislike reviews. Faster loading, a cleaner look with a background picker, and lots of fixes including favorites that now save reliably.

My Rating library sort fixed (owned grid - no more page 2/3 reset or empty results), unified API auth, performance (cached ratings.js + parallel data load), auto-removal of duplicate plugin folders, and a redesigned Letterboxd-style profile: real media names everywhere, exact-rating tooltips, clickable media to watch, 'Add a film' search/request, two-column layout with right sidebar, poster reflections, animations and a background picker.

versions.changelog: v1.8.3.36: Library jobs wait out a busy AI service (HTTP 429/503, following Retry-After) instead of failing the whole video on one rejected frame. The AI service now explains why an Intel/AMD GPU is not used (render group ID mismatch; see /doctor and /status) and runs OpenVINO on its CPU device instead of silently falling back; that part is in the AI service and needs the 1.8.3.36 Docker image. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.35: The player button no longer needs write access to Jellyfin's web folder. The plugin adds its script to index.html as Jellyfin serves the page, so Windows installs (NetworkService), the Debian package, snaps and read-only containers get the button in every browser tab. Behind a Jellyfin base URL, the Lanczos, Anime4K and WebGPU real-time engines load again. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.34: Real-time upscaling starts again in the web client. Since v1.8.3.31 it refused every video with "Video color metadata unavailable", because Jellyfin 10.9 and later no longer put the playing item in the page address; the player now reads the item from the video's stream or the web client's playback request and checks the version that plays. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.33: Redesigned in-player menu and settings page. SDR videos (DVD/SD rips, untagged 10-bit) are no longer refused as HDR in real time or in library jobs; HDR batch output keeps the model's detail; Server AI hides stale frames during outages and falls back to Lanczos when the server cannot keep up. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

v1.8.3.32: Native Jellyfin 12 build on .NET 10, aligned plugin/test dependencies, updated CI and ABI-aware release validation. Requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer. Target-hardware playback, GPU and HDR acceptance remain unverified.

versions.changelog:
Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Adgangsnøglen: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende den på (X-Emby-Token). Det ramte Subtitle Guard hårdere end de andre plugins — tolv forskellige kald sendte den gamle vej, og de svarede alle 401 på Jellyfin 12. I praksis betød det at alt det der foregår fra selve siden holdt op med at virke: workers, køen, historikken, knapperne på detaljesiden. Alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt.

Indstillingssiden kunne slet ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Det er den side hvor workers tilmeldes, så uden den kunne en ny worker ikke sættes op. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Afspil-knappen følger temaets egne farver - på ElegantFin lysegrå med sort tekst - i stedet for Jellyfins blå, også mens temaet indlæses.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden hentes meget hurtigere.

- Alle otte baggrunde blev hentet på én gang i 1920 gange skærmens pixeltæthed - 2880 px på en almindelig bærbar og 3,5 MB, mens forsiden stadig var ved at indlæse. Nu hentes kun det slide, der vises, og det næste, i en størrelse der passer til skærmen.
- Logoerne hentes også først, når deres slide er på vej.
- Indtil baggrunden er hentet, vises en sløret udgave af den.
- Størrelserne er dem, New Badges 2.8.2.0 laver på forhånd på serveren, så billederne kommer med det samme.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Intet blink i topbaren, når du scroller helt op.

- Når siden ramte toppen, skiftede Jellyfin 12 topbarens udseende og fjernede samtidig den markering, der gør den gennemsigtig over banneret. I et splitsekund kom temaets farvede bar frem og forsvandt igen. Markeringen sidder nu et sted, Jellyfin ikke rører, så topbaren forbliver gennemsigtig.
- Topbaren bliver nu gennemsigtig med det samme i stedet for at tone ud, så temaets farve ikke hænger et øjeblik i toppen, når du hopper helt op.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Mindre prikker på mobil og tablet.

- Prikkerne, der viser hvilket slide du er på, fyldte omkring halvdelen af skærmbredden på en telefon. De er nu mindre og tættere.
- Den aktive prik blev tegnet i hele sit trykfelt og var derfor en stor hvid plet. Den er nu kun lidt større end de andre.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Ingen streg under den gennemsigtige topbar.

- Skyggen, der holder topbarens knapper læsbare over banneret, sad på selve topbaren og stoppede ved dens underkant, så den tegnede omridset af den gamle topbar. Den ligger nu på banneret og toner blødt ud et godt stykke længere nede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Gennemsigtig topbar over banneret på Jellyfin 12.

- Banneret går helt op under topbaren, og topbaren er gennemsigtig, så billedet fylder hele toppen af forsiden.
- Når du scroller forbi banneret, bliver topbaren almindelig igen.
- På Favoritter, Tilføj, Kalender og alle andre sider er topbaren som før.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Banneret husker sine slides mellem besøg - de skifter alligevel kun hver 48. time - så det vises med det samme, når du åbner appen. Før blev 400 titler hentet igen ved hvert besøg, mens Jellyfins egne rækker ventede.
- Når der skal vælges nye slides, hentes kun id'erne på de 400 kandidater og derefter de 8 valgte, i stedet for alle detaljer om alle 400.
- Afspil/Fortsæt og favorit-hjertet opdateres, når Jellyfins egne rækker er indlæst, så banneret ikke sinker dem.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.0.4.0.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Kun relevant for Jellyfin 12 — på 10.11 kunne siden altid åbnes fra plugin-oversigten uanset hvad.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12. Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan KUN installeres der - Jellyfin 10.11 bliver på 2.0.4.0, som stadig virker uændret. Serveren vælger selv den rigtige.

Hvad der skulle laves om: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt i stedet. Uden det svarede serveren 401, og heroens "mest sete"-data kunne ikke hentes.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven - men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en helt ny måde, hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve. burger-knap i venstre side af app-baren på brede skærme også. Den åbner den
samme menu - med ekstra-punkterne øverst og Seerr Requests-linksene - og

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider lægger sig ikke længere oven på Jellyfins eget. Jellyfin tegner selv et baggrundsbillede i vinduer over 1000 px, og det kunne nå frem, mens vores stadig blev hentet - så lå der to lag og tonede hen over hinanden. Kontrollen sker nu lige før billedet sættes ind, i stedet for inden hentningen begynder.

Målt på Jellyfin 12: ved 1200 px vinder Jellyfins eget, ved 900 px vores. Begge dele sker, og i begge tilfælde vises nu præcis ét billede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider hentes nu i vinduets egen bredde i stedet for det dobbelte. På en skærm med skalering bad siden før om et 2560 px bredt billede til et 1268 px vindue; nu er det 1280 px - omkring en fjerdedel så mange bytes, og en størrelse serveren som regel har lavet i forvejen.

Billedet ligger bag et mørkt slør, hvor detaljerne alligevel ikke kan ses. Kort og plakater er uændrede: de ses tæt på og hentes stadig i skærmens egen opløsning.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Den natlige billedopvarmning tager nu kun titler, der er kommet til inden for de sidste 45 dage. Hele biblioteket køres igennem om søndagen, så billedstørrelser, en ny app begynder at bede om, stadig bliver lavet på forhånd.

Målt på serveren: den natlige kørsel så på 69.174 billeder for at lave 7.513 af dem og tog halvanden time, fordi resten allerede var lavet og kun blev tjekket.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Det første kort, du holder musen over efter en sideindlæsning, viser nu også forhåndsvisningen. Rækken kom på skærmen et halvt sekund før den begyndte at lytte efter musen, så den første bevægelse blev tabt - derfor virkede det næste kort med det samme, og det første bagefter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forhåndsvisningen på Fortsæt afspilning starter med det samme i stedet for efter tre sekunder, og klikker du på kortet, fortsætter afspilningen dér, hvor forhåndsvisningen er nået til.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Et klik på Fortsæt afspilning afspiller med det samme, også i browsere hvor Jellyfins fjernbetjening ikke har forbindelse - dér endte klikket før på afsnittets side.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Apps beder om lidt forskellige størrelser på hver enhed og i hvert vindue, så de fleste billeder blev lavet forfra. Størrelserne rundes nu til en kort liste, så et billede lavet til én enhed genbruges af den næste, og kvalitet over 90 sættes ned til 90 - et plakatkort fylder omkring en tredjedel mindre uden synlig forskel. Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, hvor genvejen stadig findes.

versions.changelog:
Requests og Kalender i burger-menuen.

Når Jellyfin 12 kører med den gamle skuffe - f.eks. med New Badges' burger-knap
på brede skærme - lægges de to links nu også ind der, lige under Hjem. Menuen
lukker af sig selv, når man klikker på dem.

Styres af de indstillinger, der allerede findes (Requests-fanen og
Kalender-fanen). Ingen nye indstillinger.

Kun Jellyfin 12.

- Menupillen øverst findes nu også i et halvt vindue: ikoner, med navnet på den side du er på, og et hint på resten. På en telefon ligger alt i menuen som før.
- Den valgte knap i pillen er hvid i stedet for blå.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Hele topbaren i én knapgruppe på Jellyfin 12.

- Film, Serier og dine andre biblioteker er nu med i knapgruppen, efter Favoritter og før Tilføj og Kalender. Før stod de uden for, så gruppen så ud som en bar, der stoppede halvvejs.
- Det bibliotek, du er inde i, er fyldt ud i gruppen.
- Ingen tynd kant rundt om gruppen længere - over banneret lignede den en rest af den gamle topbar. Gruppen har nu en mørk, let sløret baggrund i stedet.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Ny topbar på Jellyfin 12.

- Hjem, Favoritter, Tilføj og Kalender er samlet i én knapgruppe, hvor den side, du er på, er fyldt ud. Før var Hjem slet ikke med, og den aktive side blev kun vist med blå tekst.
- Kortere navne: "Tilføj" og "Kalender" (på engelsk "Request" og "Calendar"), så topbaren også er plads til på en bærbar.
- Tilføj og Kalender virker nu også fra andre sider end forsiden - før skete der ingenting.
- Rettet: efter at have åbnet Kalender kunne både Tilføj og Kalender stå markeret, og i sidemenuen på mobilen kunne tre punkter være markeret på én gang.
- Rettet: at skifte fra Tilføj eller Kalender til Hjem eller Favoritter kunne vise to faner oven i hinanden.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Kalenderens hukommelse - alle de titler, den har set - ligger nu i sin egen fil på serveren i stedet for i plugin-indstillingerne. Indstillingerne hentes af alle browsere ved hver sideindlæsning og var vokset til over 100 KB; nu er de få KB. Flytningen sker af sig selv, når serveren starter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 12.

"Test forbindelse"-knappen ser nu rigtig ud ved siden af Gem.

Efter sidste udgave var Gem-knappen tegnet om til Jellyfin 12's stil, men "Test forbindelse" lige under den sad tilbage i den gamle grå udgave, så de to knapper så ud til at være lige vigtige.

Den er nu en omridset knap i temaets farve — samme størrelse som Gem, men tydeligt den sekundære af de to, præcis som Jellyfin 12 selv tegner et sådant knappepar.

Kun udseende. Knappen gør nøjagtig det samme som før.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Fanerne "Tilføj Film/Serie" og "Udgivelseskalender" er flyttet med. Jellyfin 12 har lavet hele den øverste menulinje om, og den gamle fanerække findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig tegnet — så fanerne blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den rigtige menulinje sammen med Favoritter, Film og Serier, og i menuen i siden på telefon.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

description:
Syncs watched status and ratings two-way between Jellyfin and MDBList, and pushes library/collection membership to MDBList. Uses MDBList's incremental sync API (last_activities + journal) for cheap, cursor-based updates instead of full-library reconciliation on every run.

versions.changelog:
1.0.0.16: Fixed the first watched sync sending the whole Jellyfin history to MDBList if something was marked watched before it ran, and watched changes made during a sync (e.g. marking a whole season) being pushed only on the next full sync.

1.0.0.15: Fixed every activity-triggered sync running a slow full watched sync after a sync that held back unwatching items, and full watched syncs rewriting every already-synced item. The debug log now names each held-back item and each live watched change sent to MDBList.

1.0.0.14: Fixed the first watched sync sending the whole Jellyfin watch history to MDBList, which re-dated watches and could un-drop dropped shows. It now pulls MDBList's history first and only sends what MDBList doesn't have.

1.0.0.13: Fixed a watch then unwatch (or rating then removal) pulled from MDBList in the same sync only applying the first change, and changes pulled before a failed sync being pushed back on the next sync.

1.0.0.12: Fixed ratings changed or removed in MDBList being pushed back: after a sync pulled a rating from MDBList, the next sync sent it back as a new local rating, which could undo a later change there. Pulled ratings are now recorded as synced.

1.0.0.11: Fixed an item unwatched in MDBList staying watched: after a sync pulled a watched state from MDBList, the next sync pushed it back as a new local watch, undoing a later unwatch in MDBList. Pulled changes are now recorded as synced.

1.0.0.10: Scrobbles and watched sync now send each episode's own tvdb/tmdb id, so MDBList records the exact episode even when the library numbers it differently from TMDb (common for anime with TheTVDB metadata). Season/episode numbers remain the fallback.

1.0.0.9: Fixes watched/ratings sync missing episodes for shows where a different season/episode numbering is used than MDBList's own data (a common mismatch for anime, e.g. between TheTVDB and TMDb). Episodes are now matched by their own tmdb/tvdb id first, before falling back to season/episode number.

1.0.0.8: Disconnecting an MDBList account now wipes that user's sync bookkeeping, so reconnecting (same or a different account) does a clean full resync instead of diffing against a stale or foreign baseline. Adds Debug-level logging of the full-vs-incremental pull decision, cursor value, and fetched/skipped item counts for watched and ratings pulls, to make sync behavior easier to diagnose.

1.0.0.7: Fixes a rare failure mode where a sync running right after Jellyfin starts, during a library scan, or against a temporarily unreadable library could be misread as "everything was removed" and push that as a mass removal to MDBList (or, in the reverse direction, mark a batch of items unwatched locally). Removals are now only ever applied on a deliberate sync (the 24h scheduled sync or manual "Sync now"), and a suspiciously empty or oversized removal batch is held and retried on the next sync instead of applied.

1.0.0.6: Fixes hitting MDBList's rate limit on a large first sync -- requests are now paced under the server's short-window write budget, and a 429 is retried using the server's own requested wait instead of aborting the whole sync. Also fixes losing sync progress if a run is interrupted: push progress is now saved per-batch instead of only at the end, so a later failure no longer forces redoing already-pushed items.

1.0.0.5: Fixes watched-status sync: a rewatch that only updated the watch date (without changing watched/unwatched membership) could be silently dropped by the scheduled full sync, and would only reach MDBList via the immediate live-playback push.

1.0.0.4: Fixes a build issue where the plugin was compiled against a newer Jellyfin ABI (10.11.11) than the declared minimum (10.11.0), causing installs to fail with "Status: NotSupported" on Jellyfin 10.11.1 through 10.11.10.

1.0.0.3: Fixes "Disconnect" always showing a failure alert even though it always succeeded. Updates the plugin catalog icon to a full-bleed 16:9 image instead of a square logo that Jellyfin's plugin page was cropping.

1.0.0.2: Fixes the plugin catalog icon's URL -- 1.0.0.1 published one with no host, which Jellyfin couldn't fetch at all.

1.0.0.1: Fixes scheduled syncs, "Sync now", and live scrobbling only ever acting on the first linked user when multiple Jellyfin users each have their own MDBList account connected. Adds a plugin catalog icon.

1.0.0.3: Fixes "Disconnect" always showing a failure alert even though it always succeeded. Updates the plugin catalog icon to a full-bleed 16:9 image instead of a square logo that Jellyfin's plugin page was cropping.

1.0.0.2: Fixes the plugin catalog icon's URL -- 1.0.0.1 published one with no host, which Jellyfin couldn't fetch at all.

1.0.0.1: Fixes scheduled syncs, "Sync now", and live scrobbling only ever acting on the first linked user when multiple Jellyfin users each have their own MDBList account connected. Adds a plugin catalog icon.

1.0.0.0: Initial release. Two-way sync of watched status and ratings, push-only collection sync, live playback scrobbling to MDBList's /scrobble endpoints, OAuth device-code authentication, incremental cursor-based pulls with automatic full-reconciliation fallback, a 24h scheduled full sync plus a 15-minute activity-gated cheap poll, and a config page for connecting your account and choosing what to sync.

1.0.0.11: Fixed an item unwatched in MDBList staying watched: after a sync pulled a watched state from MDBList, the next sync pushed it back as a new local watch, undoing a later unwatch in MDBList. Pulled changes are now recorded as synced.

1.0.0.10: Scrobbles and watched sync now send each episode's own tvdb/tmdb id, so MDBList records the exact episode even when the library numbers it differently from TMDb (common for anime with TheTVDB metadata). Season/episode numbers remain the fallback.

1.0.0.9: Fixes watched/ratings sync missing episodes for shows where a different season/episode numbering is used than MDBList's own data (a common mismatch for anime, e.g. between TheTVDB and TMDb). Episodes are now matched by their own tmdb/tvdb id first, before falling back to season/episode number.

1.0.0.8: Disconnecting an MDBList account now wipes that user's sync bookkeeping, so reconnecting (same or a different account) does a clean full resync instead of diffing against a stale or foreign baseline. Adds Debug-level logging of the full-vs-incremental pull decision, cursor value, and fetched/skipped item counts for watched and ratings pulls, to make sync behavior easier to diagnose.

1.0.0.7: Fixes a rare failure mode where a sync running right after Jellyfin starts, during a library scan, or against a temporarily unreadable library could be misread as "everything was removed" and push that as a mass removal to MDBList (or, in the reverse direction, mark a batch of items unwatched locally). Removals are now only ever applied on a deliberate sync (the 24h scheduled sync or manual "Sync now"), and a suspiciously empty or oversized removal batch is held and retried on the next sync instead of applied.

1.0.0.6: Fixes hitting MDBList's rate limit on a large first sync -- requests are now paced under the server's short-window write budget, and a 429 is retried using the server's own requested wait instead of aborting the whole sync. Also fixes losing sync progress if a run is interrupted: push progress is now saved per-batch instead of only at the end, so a later failure no longer forces redoing already-pushed items.

versions.changelog:
## [0.26.26.0] - 2026-10-18

### 🚀 Features

- Skip segments from a stream's named chapters with RemuxDB on (#300)
- Look segments up again and read chapters of rows probed before (#303)
- List a stream that probed to a short clip after the others (#304)
- Add a title to the library when its request is approved in Seerr (#306)
- Show how to set up the seerr webhook on the settings page and in the readme (#307)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Keep an episode edit made while its series refresh runs (#301)
- Leave a local series that is being scanned to the next tree sync run (#302)
- Keep a title deleted right after it was added from coming back (#308)
- List a catalog's moved movies in its library at once (#309)

### ⚡ Performance

- Leave a probed short stream and a placeholder unprobed at play (#305)

## [0.26.25.0] - 2026-10-16

### 🚀 Features

- Settings page in tabs, with a setup assistant for a new install (#294)
- Play the next stream when the first one does not start (#206)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Stop listing a stream's subtitle once its file is deleted (#295)
- Leave a title in a library the user cannot open out of their search (#296)
- Keep a library's movies when its folder is reported leaving twice (#297)
- Keep a subtitle's index when an older subtitle file is deleted (#298)
- Keep an inserted title's streams linked after its first refresh (#299)

## [0.26.24.0] - 2026-10-15

### 🚀 Features

- Add a gelato copy of a title held as a file from a search inside a gelato library (#289)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Answer a progress report for an item that no longer exists (#280)
- Give two catalogs of one name a collection each (#281)
- Give a local series' added episodes ids of their own (#282)
- Probe and fill in a stream row that lost its tracks (#283)
- Look a movie up by its imdb id when tmdb has no movie under the addon's id (#284)
- Count a request being torn down as no request in task reads (#285)
- Hand jellyfin a path-safe id for an addon subtitle (#286)
- Save playback reports for a deleted stream row on its movie (#287)
- Download a stream row's missing subtitle once when two downloads meet (#288)
- Release a movie without a digital date once tmdb lists a watch provider (#290)
- Offer subtitles the addon sends with a three-letter b code (#291)
- Download from the next stream when a title's first link is dead (#292)
- Download a probed stream's subtitles after the probe, not inside the playback (#293)

## [0.26.23.0] - 2026-10-13

### 🚀 Features

- Support catalog to library mapping (#253)
- Support binge groups in episodes (#276)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Serve a download that names no user (#278)
- Keep gelato items when their library folder is removed (#279)

### ⚡ Performance

- Fewer queries for listings with stream rows (#277)

## [0.26.22.1] - 2026-10-09

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Pre-probe only opened pages and probe a source once (#262)
- Answer a movie/episode's segments with those of the stream it plays (#263)
- Order stream sync and reset by a sequence (#268)
- Share a prepared playback source from the end of its preparation (#267)
- List a local episode once in an extended series tree (#270)
- Take search results into the collection or playlist they are added to (#269)
- Find the stream listed under the item's id by its own id too (#271)
- Report one search total on every page (#272)
- Offer a subtitle saved on a movie's or episode's page with its streams (#273)

### ⚡ Performance

- Cache playback source preperation once for its streaming requests (#264)
- Faster listings, search and opening a movie from search (#274)

## [0.26.22.0] - 2026-10-02

### 🚀 Features

- Probe streams before playback (#257)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fetch intro segments before the first play of a remuxdb stream (#256)

### ⚡ Performance

- Fetch a movie's tmdb id and release dates in one request (#259)
- Find stream rows and stremio ids through indexes (#258)

## [0.26.21.1] - 2026-10-01

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Probe remuxdb streams that lack a video bitrate before playback (#255)

## [0.26.21.0] - 2026-10-01

### 🚀 Features

- Fill in stream media info from remuxdb (#251)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Scheduled tasks failing when started from the dashboard (#247)
- Seed gelato folders once when lookups race (#248)

### ⚙️ Miscellaneous Tasks

- Various housekeeping tasks (#246)
- Remove p2p torrent streaming (#250)

## [0.26.20.0] - 2026-09-22

### 🚀 Features

- Scope library search correctly (#243)
- Aiometadata v3 support (#244)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Support canonical ids for breadcrumbs (#241)
- Dedupe search results (#242)

### ⚡ Performance

- Speed up search results (#245)

## [0.26.19.3] - 2026-09-21

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Let user data actions materialize a search result (#227)
- Keep downloads working when the token is an API key (#234)
- Leave the library's own episodes and seasons out of the tree clean-up (#235)
- Keep the addon stream URL out of client-facing responses (#236)
- Materialize a search result opened with an API key (#237)

versions.changelog: If the plugin stopped working with "The poster overlay state file ... could not be read", this release is for you. The state file is now written atomically, so a server that dies mid-write can no longer leave it empty - which is what happened on the reference server when the VM was killed during the nightly run. An image uploaded just before a crash is now recognised on the next run, and a cached original without a record is never overwritten. New task "Rebuild poster overlay state": run it with the dry run on first. It rebuilds a record only where drawing today's badges onto the cached original gives the cover on the item again, and lists everything else by name without touching it. Do not delete a damaged state file - the old error message advised that, and it was wrong.

Nothing changes visibly in this one. The preview picker on the settings page now tells the server explicitly not to substitute collections for the films inside them when searching. That was already the behaviour, but only because Jellyfin happens to switch it off for searches by itself - and because the search box never queries with fewer than two characters. Neither is something this plugin controls, so it now says what it means. Badges, rendering and the scheduled task are untouched.

The report about folder names that disagree with the video stream over HDR is now a setting, and it is off by default. It only says something if your folder names carry release tags - if you name folders "Film (Year)", every HDR title would be counted as a disagreement. Turn it on under Operation if the tags are there. The badges follow the video stream either way, with the report on or off.

Names the file behind "the image could not be decoded" instead of only the film, so a broken cover can be found without searching by hand - and fixes a case where that message could not be reached at all, because the renderer threw on a file its decoder cannot open rather than reporting it. The HDR/DV disagreement between folder name and video stream is now summarised once per run instead of printed for every film: it is the ordinary case, not an exception, and it was burying the messages worth reading. The v12 build now targets Jellyfin 12.0.0 rather than a release candidate.

Fixes a badge that could not be taken off again. When an item lost its last badge - a duplicate was deleted, or it never really had a twin - the plugin was supposed to put the untouched cover back, and never did: the restore asked for a lock its own caller was already holding, then failed silently. A run with 222 items to restore restored none of them and reported a missing cache that was present. If your library carries labels that no longer apply, the next nightly run clears them.

Fixes the audio badge appearing on films that have no second copy at all.

Peers were matched by any shared provider id, which swept in TmdbCollection - an id every film of a series carries. All fifteen Star Wars films therefore counted as copies of one another, their audio formats differed, and a badge appeared where the rule says there should be none. Only ids that name a title are used now: IMDb, TMDb, TVDB and the custom id an NFO can set.

Also fixes the badge never appearing in the previous version, where copies were grouped by Jellyfin's presentation key. That key groups the rows of a series, but for a film it falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Fixes the audio badge never appearing. It was grouping copies of a film by Jellyfin's presentation key, which groups the rows of a series but not of a film: for a film that key falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it and the badge was skipped every time. Copies are now matched by provider id.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, and describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups holding more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of languages, best first - the first one any track carries wins. This matters more than it sounds: 437 films carry several languages in different formats, typically a German AC3 beside an English DTS, and taking the best track badges such a film "DTS", which is true about the file and about a track its owner never selects. Setting a language therefore draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent.

Spelling is forgiving because the server is asked rather than a table in the plugin: "de", "ger", "deu" and "German" all name one language, for every language Jellyfin knows. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says.

Within the chosen language only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film. The label carries as much as the job needs: where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected - the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody switched off stays switched off.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of ISO language codes. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says. Spelling is forgiving, since ISO 639-2 gives several languages two codes and files in the wild use both.

Setting a language draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent: two of the groups it stops badging differ only in a track in a language nobody at that library listens to, while both preferred tracks are identical.

Within the chosen language only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film. The label carries as much as the job needs: where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected - the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody switched off stays switched off.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - and draws it only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.
